Double Peaking Phenomena in Pharmacokinetic Disposition Revisited. Multiple peaking in pharmacokinetics refers to the occurrence of two or more peaks of drug plasma concentrations following a single dose administration. It complicates interpretation of pharmacokinetics parameters and influences clinical decision-making regarding drug efficacy and bioequivalence. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic evaluation of alternative pomalidomide dosing regimens in the treatment of multiple myeloma. Standard pomalidomide dosing (4 mg/day for 21 of 28 days) achieved the most robust pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) effects. Daily dosing with pomalidomide 2 mg is a safe alternative for patients at risk of toxicity; alternate-day dosing was less effective.
